name: Varsen RadSeal Contamination Suit Mk-IV
description:
A full-body radiation containment suit in dull ochre with charcoal seam tape, constructed from trilaminate lead-weave bonded to a breathable rad-absorb membrane. Shelf workers near the old reactor spillways wear these until the seams crack and the hood seal whistles. Pre-owned units show yellowing at the chest bib and scorch rings around the boot cuffs.

The hood integrates a replaceable carbon-filter cartridge and a polycarbonate face shield scratched from years of particulate exposure. Wrist and ankle closures use double-roll gasketing. Seams are RF-welded, not stitched.
functionality: Rated for low-to-mid ionizing radiation exposure up to 8-hour shift duration; replaceable hood filter cartridges extend usable life; double-roll gasket closures at wrists, ankles, and hood neck ring prevent particulate ingress; boot soles are acid-resistant nitrile.
what_it_says: You work somewhere that will kill you slowly, and you know it.
story_hooks: A suit returned to a Shelf secondhand stall still has a name written in marker inside the hood — and that person was reported dead six months ago.
A Tier 2 maintenance tech discovers their RadSeal Mk-IV is three certification cycles out of date — their supervisor has been falsifying inspection records.
The carbon filter cartridges have been counterfeited; a runner needs to trace the supply chain before the next shift rotation kills a dozen workers.
